source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Check divisibility by 10, 5, and 2 from the final digit.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Divisibility by 10 is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Check divisibility by 10, 5, and 2 from the final digit' is answered as divisibility by 10 rather than final digit.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: final digit still holds here even though 125 is not divisible by 10 because it does not end in 0, even though it ends in 5 is missing from the stem — on the item about Check divisibility by 10, 5, and 2 from the final.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The final digit rule also covers this: divisibility by 4 and 8, so it is not an exception — on the item about Check divisibility by 10, 5, and 2 from the final.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is final digit because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Check divisibility by 10, 5, and 2 from the final digit' as the operative test.

intelligence.enrichment: A whole number is divisible by 10 if it ends in 0, by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5, and by 2 if it ends in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.
